definitions.title: Guided Setup
definitions.summary: Configure Prisma Generator for your printer and learn its essential utility controls.

steps.title: Configure your printer
steps.body: Let's begin by configuring Prisma Generator for your printer. Open Printer Configuration.

steps.title: Review printer setup
steps.body: Update the printer profile to match the bed dimensions and number of AMS units that your printer has, then close the Printer Configuration window.

steps.title: Select the active nozzle
steps.body: Confirm that the selected nozzle matches the nozzle installed on your printer, and change it if necessary. Prisma uses this choice when evaluating whether model features can be printed reliably.

steps.title: Model Libraries
steps.body: A Model Library supplies Prisma with calibrated filament models. Prisma includes a library containing many common filaments. Use Manage later when you want to install a library published by Prisma Calibration or change the active Model Library. Changing the active library restarts Prisma Generator, so leave it unchanged during this guide.

steps.title: Active Filaments
steps.body: Active Filaments chooses which filaments Prisma may use. Mark filaments you do not own or use as inactive so they are excluded from palette tools. Your choices persist between sessions.

steps.title: Choose a theme
steps.body: This button changes Prisma Generator’s color theme. If the current theme is not the one you prefer, choose another.

steps.title: Temporary files
steps.body: Prisma automatically clears temporary working data when a new session starts. Clear Temp Files lets you remove it manually during or at the end of the current session.

steps.title: Help & Guides
steps.body: You can reopen Guided Setup and launch other available guides from Help & Guides.

steps.title: Ready to create
steps.body: Guided Setup is complete, and Prisma Generator is ready to use. Happy printing!

followup.text: If you are new to Prisma Generator, continue with the guided introduction to its features and workflow.
followup.label: Start Prisma Generator Basics

definitions.title: Prisma Generator Basics
definitions.summary: Create, compare, inspect, and export a complete tutorial lithophane.

detours.label: Image Controls
detours.description: Explore framing, appearance, borders, and physical-size controls.

steps.title: Adjustments panel
steps.body:
The Adjustments panel sets the lithophane’s shape and physical size, how the photograph fits inside it, and the photograph’s appearance.

We will look at its Size and Image controls next.

steps.title: Aspect-ratio choices
steps.body:
The Size tab offers W×H for independent dimensions, Ratio for a custom ratio, Image for the source ratio, and common 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, and 1:1 ratios.

Landscape and Portrait set the canvas orientation. Feel free to try these controls; the guide does not require a particular choice at this point.

steps.title: Crop-fit shortcuts
steps.body:
The first Crop Fit button resets the image zoom and centers it. The other two resize the frame to use the source image’s full width or full height.

Each button provides a quick way to establish an initial crop; you can continue refining the framing afterward. Feel free to try all three.

steps.title: Interactive framing
steps.body:
Use the mouse wheel over the editor to zoom, then drag the image to choose what remains inside the frame.

Scale and Rotate provide precise controls, and the nearby buttons rotate by 90 degrees or flip the source. Experiment if you like; Reset will remove these changes.

steps.title: Physical dimensions
steps.body:
Width and Height set the lithophane’s physical dimensions in millimeters. The lock buttons determine whether changing one dimension also updates the other.

You do not need to change these values yet. The guide will ask you to set the tutorial dimensions after this tour.

steps.title: Optional printed border
steps.body:
The Border control adds a raised frame around the lithophane, printed in the same color as the cap. It can provide a finished edge and extra support.

Turn the border on if you want to preview it, then turn it off before continuing.

steps.title: Resolution summary
steps.body:
Image Size is the source image’s resolution. Print Size is the physical size of the lithophane. Rendered Size is the pixel grid that Prisma will solve.

A larger canvas or a smaller Solve Pitch (the physical spacing between pixels in Prisma’s solver grid) creates more solve pixels and requires more time.

steps.title: Open the Image controls
steps.body: Select Image at the top of the Adjustments panel to open the image-adjustment controls. The guide will continue automatically.

steps.title: Image appearance
steps.body:
B/W and Color choose the overall image mode.

Exposure changes brightness; Contrast separates light and dark values; Highlight and Shadow target the brightest and darkest areas. Tint, Saturation, and Temperature adjust color balance and intensity.

Feel free to experiment with these controls. You will reset them before setting the tutorial canvas.

detours.label: Palette Tools
detours.description: Explore filament eligibility and build a temporary Manual palette.

steps.title: Auto-Suggest filaments
steps.body:
Every active filament that can be used for color is already selected here.

This does not add every selected filament to one palette. It tells Auto-Suggest which filaments it may combine when building suggestions.

The filament reserved for the white base and cap cannot also be selected as a color. Leave the current selection unchanged for this guide.

steps.title: Build a Manual palette
steps.body:
The Manual builder is now open.

Choose one or more colored filaments in any order, then select Add to Deck. The guide will continue after your new palette appears in the sidebar Deck.

steps.title: Remove the Manual palette
steps.body:
This is the temporary palette you just added.

Select its × button once; it changes to ! to ask for confirmation. Select it a second time to remove the card.

The two suggested tutorial palettes will remain.

detours.label: Settings
detours.description: Explore solver, White Cap, and Advanced settings without changing the tutorial profile.

steps.title: Solver settings
steps.body:
Preprocessing can reduce noise, smooth printable-scale features, or reshape tone and saturation before solving.

The Color Solver controls how Prisma divides the image and searches for printable filament recipes.

Difficult photographs may benefit from these tools. Leave them unchanged for this tutorial image.

steps.title: White Cap
steps.body:
The White Cap covers the color stack.

Its boundary portion keeps the print structurally covered; its detail portion can restore fine appearance information. Smoothing and depth determine how that material is distributed.

Keep the tutorial profile’s White Cap settings unchanged for this guide.

steps.title: Advanced settings
steps.body:
Turn Advanced on.

It reveals less frequently changed controls without changing their values. Look around, then turn Advanced off again to continue.

detours.label: Preview
detours.description: Explore Solve History, result views, inspection, and captured settings.

steps.title: Solve History
steps.body:
Solve History contains one card for each completed run. Selecting cards controls which results appear in the comparison area.

Each card also provides captured settings and actions for saving or removing the run.

steps.title: Preview views
steps.body:
Predicted estimates the illuminated result. White Cap separates the Total, Boundary, and Detail cap geometry. Color Regions contains Color Ceiling and Recipe Viewer.

Top Surface shows the final combined surface. Explorer examines materials around a selected height. Advanced contains the diagnostic Thickness Maps and Highpass views.

Visit any view you like. A later guide will explain these tools in depth.

steps.title: Inspect the previews
steps.body:
Preview images can be opened for larger inspection.

Subview controls change which part of a solve is shown, and contextual controls appear only where relevant. Feel free to inspect the runs or move among views.

steps.title: Run settings and saves
steps.body:
A run’s Settings view records exactly what was captured when its solve began.

Use These Settings applies that snapshot as the current temporary Settings Profile for a future solve.

Solve History is session-only unless a run is explicitly saved; Load opens Saved Runs.

You do not need to save or load a run during this guide.

detours.label: Export Choices
detours.description: Learn what output format, mesh method, and mesh detail control.

steps.title: Export choices
steps.body:
Output format chooses one bundled 3MF or separate STL files. Mesh method controls how the solved surface becomes printable geometry, and Mesh detail controls reconstruction scale for the field-derived method.

These choices affect file packaging and mesh construction; they do not repeat or change the solve.

steps.title: Prisma Generator Basics
steps.body:
This guide will show you the basic steps for converting an image into the 3D meshes used to print a color lithophane.

Along the way, you will learn how Prisma Generator organizes images, palettes, settings, solve results, and print files. You can end this guide at any time.

steps.title: Terminology
steps.body:
There are two terms you should know before continuing:

• A **palette** is a small set of colored filaments that can be layered together to produce the colors in a finished lithophane. They act like “primary colors” that Prisma combines to reproduce the colors in the source image.

• A **solve** is Prisma’s process for deciding how to layer the filaments in a palette to recreate the appearance of an image.

steps.title: The Generator workflow
steps.body:
Prisma’s numbered workflow moves from a source image to printable files:

Image → Palette → Preview → Export

Settings are available throughout the workflow and affect the next solve. You can start a solve from any workflow page; it uses the prepared image, active palette, and current settings at the moment it begins.

Each stage will be explained in more detail as you move through this guide.

steps.title: Select the Tutorial Printer profile
steps.body:
This guide uses the Tutorial Printer profile to ensure that all learners get the same experience.

Select Tutorial Printer from the Active printer list. If it is already active, the guide will continue automatically.

steps.title: Confirm the tutorial nozzle
steps.body:
Smaller nozzles can produce higher-quality lithophanes, but they take longer to solve and print. This guide uses a 0.4 mm nozzle to save time while you learn the basics.

Confirm that the nozzle selector is set to 0.4 mm. If necessary, change the selection, then select Next.

steps.title: Image: prepare the source
steps.body:
The Image page is where you prepare the source image Prisma will reproduce as a lithophane.

Here you choose an image, frame it within a physical canvas, and adjust its appearance.

The adjusted image represents how you want the finished lithophane to look. Prisma uses it when recommending palettes and as the visual target it attempts to recreate during a solve.

steps.title: Adding images to the library
steps.body:
The Image Library contains the source images you can use to create lithophanes.

Use Add Image to import one or more images, or copy image files directly into Prisma’s Images folder. Open Folder opens that folder in your file browser.

steps.title: Updating and expanding the library
steps.body:
Prisma Generator checks the Images folder for changes whenever it starts.

If you add, remove, or replace files in that folder while Prisma Generator is running, select Refresh to update the Image Library.

Use the button to the right of Refresh to expand or collapse the library when you need more room to browse.

steps.title: Select the tutorial image
steps.body:
For this guide, we will use **{{tutorialImage}}** as the source image.

Select it to continue.

steps.title: Preview and Adjustments
steps.body:
Preview shows how the source image is framed and updates as you change the canvas, crop, or appearance.

Adjustments controls the lithophane’s shape, physical size, framing, and image appearance.

These changes affect future solves but never modify the original image.

steps.title: Reset the image controls
steps.body:
Reset restores the Size and Image controls in the Adjustments panel to their defaults.

Please click Reset to clear any changes you may have tried and to continue in this guide.

steps.title: Set the tutorial canvas
steps.body:
Set the physical canvas to exactly 90 × 120 mm (Width 90, Height 120). You may use either the W×H or Image options for Aspect Ratio for this tutorial image. Using the same canvas size keeps the tutorial results consistent for everyone.

If you experimented with the border, please turn it off before continuing.

Select Next when the canvas is 90 × 120 mm and the border is off.

steps.title: Continue to Palette
steps.body: The source image is ready. Open Palette to choose the colored filaments Prisma may use.

steps.title: Palette: choose your filaments
steps.body:
A **palette** is the set of filaments Prisma will use to recreate the colors in an image.

You can use the tools found on the Palette page to build palettes manually or to have Prisma automatically create palettes tailored to your image.

steps.title: Building a palette
steps.body:
Auto-Suggest recommends palettes whose filaments will do a good job of reproducing the colors in the source image when they are combined.

Its recommendations can only include filaments that have been selected in this panel. Deselecting a filament prevents Auto-Suggest from including it in the palettes.

Please note that whichever filament is currently assigned to be used for the base and white cap of your lithophane cannot be included in palettes. You will learn more about this later in the guide.

steps.title: Auto-Suggest controls
steps.body:
**Palette colors** specifies the exact number of colored filaments in each suggested palette, while **Suggestions** controls how many palettes Auto-Suggest will return.

The Solve mode selector changes the type of palette that Auto-Suggest will recommend. You should only change this to Luminance if you are also using Prisma’s Luminance solve mode. You will learn more about solve modes later.

steps.title: Suggest palettes
steps.body:
Auto-Suggest will compare combinations of the selected filaments with the source image and return ranked palette cards. This may take some time; the progress display shows its status and lets you cancel if needed.

For this guide, confirm that Palette colors is set to exactly 3 and Suggestions is at least 2.

Select Suggest Palettes to continue.

steps.title: Suggested palettes
steps.body:
Suggested cards show their filaments and image-specific metrics. Metrics help rank palettes under the model, but only partly correspond to whether a real lithophane looks good.

For this guide, use the two highest-ranked results: {{paletteA}} and {{paletteB}}. Add both to the Palette Deck.

steps.title: The Palette Deck
steps.body:
The sidebar Deck contains palettes ready to solve.

Load retrieves a saved palette, and Clear removes all Deck cards after confirmation.

Selecting a card makes it active. A card menu can create a Manual variant or save it; × removes only that card.

steps.title: Activate first palette
steps.body: Select {{paletteA}} in the Deck. The highlighted card is the active palette used by the next solve.

steps.title: Settings: control the solve
steps.body:
Settings controls how Prisma converts the prepared image and active palette into a printable layer plan.

It covers physical structure, image preprocessing, solver behavior, and the white cap.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.body:
This guide uses the prepared tutorial defaults.

Open Settings to review them and continue.

steps.title: Profiles and Essentials
steps.body:
A Settings Profile is a reusable collection of solve settings. Tutorial Basics is a temporary copy of the built-in Basic profile with Solve Pitch set to 0.4 mm for faster tutorial solves.

Essentials contains Solve Mode, Solve Pitch, Max Total Thickness, Layer Height, White Base/Cap Filament, and Base Thickness. The diagram shows the base, color layers, and white cap.

Profiles… is where you load other Settings Profiles. Leave Tutorial Basics unchanged and select Next.

steps.title: Close Settings
steps.body:
Settings are captured when a solve begins, so every run retains the values that produced it.

Close Settings to continue.

steps.title: Solve: first palette
steps.body:
Select Solve.

A solve can be started from any workflow page. It uses the prepared image, active palette, and current settings at the moment it begins. Prisma will move to Preview while it works.

steps.title: Preview: compare and inspect results
steps.body:
Preview is where Prisma collects completed solve runs so you can compare their predicted appearance, inspect their printable structures, and review the settings that produced them.

A run is one solve result created from a particular image, palette, and collection of settings.

We will create a second run before exploring the available inspection tools.

steps.title: First solve result
steps.body:
You are now in Preview. The completed run appears in Solve History, while its predicted result appears in the comparison area.

These two regions stay linked as you add and select runs.

steps.title: Activate the second palette
steps.body: Without leaving Preview, select {{paletteB}} in the Deck. The guide will continue when it becomes the active palette.

steps.title: Solve the second palette
steps.body:
Select Solve again.

Solve is available throughout the workflow and uses the active palette, so you do not need to leave Preview. This second run will give you two results to compare.

steps.title: Compare the solves
steps.body:
Both guide runs should now be selected and displayed side by side in the comparison area.

This is where you judge the visible differences between palettes. Select Next after looking at both results.

steps.title: Open Export
steps.body: Export creates files for one completed run at a time. Open Export.

steps.title: Export: create print files
steps.body:
Export converts one completed run into files for slicing and printing.

Here you choose the run and how its geometry should be packaged. Prisma then creates the meshes, filament instructions, and mesh report from that run’s stored data.

Exporting does not repeat the solve or change the completed run.

steps.title: Select the export run
steps.body:
Export begins with one completed run.

Select the run made with {{paletteA}}. Its preview and dimensions confirm which solve will be exported.

steps.title: Print-file options
steps.body:
Output format chooses one bundled 3MF or individual STL files. Mesh method chooses how the solved surface becomes geometry. Mesh detail controls reconstruction scale for the field-derived method.

Use Single 3MF file, Field-derived white cap, and 4x balanced, then select Next.

steps.title: Generate Print Files
steps.body:
Select Generate Print Files.

Prisma builds 3D model files and filament-loading or swap instructions from the selected run’s stored data.

steps.title: Files are already saved
steps.body:
The export record preserves its options and lists generated files, filament-loading or swap instructions, and the mesh report.

These files are already saved in the Output folder shown below. Use Open Folder to view them.

Download .zip creates a packaged copy in a location you choose. Use it only when you want a copy outside the workspace.

steps.title: Project complete
steps.body:
You completed Prisma Generator’s normal workflow: selected the Tutorial Printer profile, prepared a source image, built and compared palettes, reviewed settings, made two solves, inspected Preview, and generated print files.

Your previous Settings Profile will be restored when this guide closes. The Tutorial Printer profile and its 0.4 mm nozzle will remain active. Before starting your own project, select the profile and nozzle for your printer.

Happy printing!

definitions.title: Preview Guide
definitions.summary: Create two tutorial solves, then compare and inspect their results.

steps.title: Confirm the tutorial nozzle
steps.body:
Smaller nozzles can produce higher-quality lithophanes, but they take longer to solve and print. This guide uses a 0.4 mm nozzle to save time while you learn the basics.

Confirm that the nozzle selector is set to 0.4 mm. If necessary, change the selection, then select Next.

steps.title: Select the tutorial image
steps.body:
For this guide, we will use **{{tutorialImage}}** as the source image.

Select it to continue.

steps.title: Reset the image controls
steps.body:
Reset restores the Size and Image controls in the Adjustments panel to their defaults.

Please click Reset to clear any changes you may have tried and to continue in this guide.

steps.title: Set the tutorial canvas
steps.body:
Set the physical canvas to exactly 90 × 120 mm (Width 90, Height 120). You may use either the W×H or Image options for Aspect Ratio for this tutorial image. Using the same canvas size keeps the tutorial results consistent for everyone.

If you experimented with the border, please turn it off before continuing.

Select Next when the canvas is 90 × 120 mm and the border is off.

steps.title: Continue to Palette
steps.body: The source image is ready. Open Palette to choose the colored filaments Prisma may use.

steps.title: Building a palette
steps.body:
Auto-Suggest recommends palettes whose filaments will do a good job of reproducing the colors in the source image when they are combined.

Its recommendations can only include filaments that have been selected in this panel. Deselecting a filament prevents Auto-Suggest from including it in the palettes.

Please note that whichever filament is currently assigned to be used for the base and white cap of your lithophane cannot be included in palettes. You will learn more about this later in the guide.

steps.title: Auto-Suggest controls
steps.body:
**Palette colors** specifies the exact number of colored filaments in each suggested palette, while **Suggestions** controls how many palettes Auto-Suggest will return.

The Solve mode selector changes the type of palette that Auto-Suggest will recommend. You should only change this to Luminance if you are also using Prisma’s Luminance solve mode. You will learn more about solve modes later.

steps.title: Suggest palettes
steps.body:
Auto-Suggest will compare combinations of the selected filaments with the source image and return ranked palette cards. This may take some time; the progress display shows its status and lets you cancel if needed.

For this guide, confirm that Palette colors is set to exactly 3 and Suggestions is at least 2.

Select Suggest Palettes to continue.

steps.title: Suggested palettes
steps.body:
Suggested cards show their filaments and image-specific metrics. Metrics help rank palettes under the model, but only partly correspond to whether a real lithophane looks good.

For this guide, use the two highest-ranked results: {{paletteA}} and {{paletteB}}. Add both to the Palette Deck.

steps.title: Activate first palette
steps.body: Select {{paletteA}} in the Deck. The highlighted card is the active palette used by the next solve.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.body:
This guide uses the prepared tutorial defaults.

Open Settings to review them and continue.

steps.title: Profiles and Essentials
steps.body:
A Settings Profile is a reusable collection of solve settings. Tutorial Basics is a temporary copy of the built-in Basic profile with Solve Pitch set to 0.4 mm for faster tutorial solves.

Essentials contains Solve Mode, Solve Pitch, Max Total Thickness, Layer Height, White Base/Cap Filament, and Base Thickness. The diagram shows the base, color layers, and white cap.

Profiles… is where you load other Settings Profiles. Leave Tutorial Basics unchanged and select Next.

steps.title: Close Settings
steps.body:
Settings are captured when a solve begins, so every run retains the values that produced it.

Close Settings to continue.

steps.title: Solve: first palette
steps.body:
Select Solve.

A solve can be started from any workflow page. It uses the prepared image, active palette, and current settings at the moment it begins. Prisma will move to Preview while it works.

steps.title: Preview: compare and inspect results
steps.body:
Preview is where Prisma collects completed solve runs so you can compare their predicted appearance, inspect their printable structures, and review the settings that produced them.

A run is one solve result created from a particular image, palette, and collection of settings.

We will create a second run before exploring the available inspection tools.

steps.title: First solve result
steps.body:
You are now in Preview. The completed run appears in Solve History, while its predicted result appears in the comparison area.

These two regions stay linked as you add and select runs.

steps.title: Activate the second palette
steps.body: Without leaving Preview, select {{paletteB}} in the Deck. The guide will continue when it becomes the active palette.

steps.title: Solve the second palette
steps.body:
Select Solve again.

Solve is available throughout the workflow and uses the active palette, so you do not need to leave Preview. This second run will give you two results to compare.

steps.title: Compare the solves
steps.body:
Both guide runs should now be selected and displayed side by side in the comparison area.

This is where you judge the visible differences between palettes. Select Next after looking at both results.

steps.title: Solve History
steps.body:
Solve History contains one card for each completed run. Selecting cards controls which results appear in the comparison area.

Each card also provides captured settings and actions for saving or removing the run.

steps.title: Preview views
steps.body:
Predicted estimates the illuminated result. White Cap separates the Total, Boundary, and Detail cap geometry. Color Regions contains Color Ceiling and Recipe Viewer.

Top Surface shows the final combined surface. Explorer examines materials around a selected height. Advanced contains the diagnostic Thickness Maps and Highpass views.

Visit any view you like. A later guide will explain these tools in depth.

steps.title: Inspect the previews
steps.body:
Preview images can be opened for larger inspection.

Subview controls change which part of a solve is shown, and contextual controls appear only where relevant. Feel free to inspect the runs or move among views.

steps.title: Run settings and saves
steps.body:
A run’s Settings view records exactly what was captured when its solve began.

Use These Settings applies that snapshot as the current temporary Settings Profile for a future solve.

Solve History is session-only unless a run is explicitly saved; Load opens Saved Runs.

You do not need to save or load a run during this guide.

steps.title: Preview Guide complete
steps.body: You created two tutorial solves and explored comparison, Solve History, result views, and captured settings.

definitions.title: Export Guide
definitions.summary: Create a tutorial solve and generate its print files.

catalog.note: Creates one tutorial solve and print files.

steps.body:

Select Tutorial Printer from the Active printer list. If it is already active, the guide will continue automatically.

steps.title: Open Export
steps.body: Export creates files for one completed run at a time. Open Export.

steps.title: Export: create print files
steps.body:
Export converts one completed run into files for slicing and printing.

Here you choose the run and how its geometry should be packaged. Prisma then creates the meshes, filament instructions, and mesh report from that run’s stored data.

Exporting does not repeat the solve or change the completed run.

steps.title: Select the export run
steps.body:
Export begins with one completed run.

Select the run made with {{paletteA}}. Its preview and dimensions confirm which solve will be exported.

steps.title: Export choices
steps.body:
Output format chooses one bundled 3MF or separate STL files. Mesh method controls how the solved surface becomes printable geometry, and Mesh detail controls reconstruction scale for the field-derived method.

These choices affect file packaging and mesh construction; they do not repeat or change the solve.

steps.title: Print-file options
steps.body:
Output format chooses one bundled 3MF or individual STL files. Mesh method chooses how the solved surface becomes geometry. Mesh detail controls reconstruction scale for the field-derived method.

Use Single 3MF file, Field-derived white cap, and 4x balanced, then select Next.

steps.title: Generate Print Files
steps.body:
Select Generate Print Files.

Prisma builds 3D model files and filament-loading or swap instructions from the selected run’s stored data.

steps.title: Files are already saved
steps.body:
The export record preserves its options and lists generated files, filament-loading or swap instructions, and the mesh report.

These files are already saved in the Output folder shown below. Use Open Folder to view them.

Download .zip creates a packaged copy in a location you choose. Use it only when you want a copy outside the workspace.

steps.title: Export Guide complete
steps.body: You created a tutorial solve, generated its print files, and reviewed where Prisma stores the resulting files and instructions.

steps.body: You can reopen Guided Setup and launch other available guides here whenever you need them.

steps.title: Prisma's workflow
steps.body: These numbered tabs follow the normal path from choosing an image through exporting a finished lithophane.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.body: Select Settings. This guide continues after Prisma confirms that the drawer opened.

steps.title: Settings can be identified in place
steps.body: This is White-point rescale. The guide frames the existing row without changing the setting or layout.

steps.title: Guides can follow the workflow
steps.body: Prisma can reveal another part of the interface and keep the explanation attached across different window sizes and zoom levels.
